Test Description: Validates the default reset values and masked read/write behavior of GPIO GP0 registers 8 through 27. The test checks that readable bits return the documented reset values (with bit 0 ignored), and that after applying multiple write patterns, readable and writable bits reflect the programmed values while non-writable readable bits retain their defaults.
Meta Test Description: The testcase exercises a two-part flow: (1) default/reset-value verification and (2) masked write/readback verification across multiple patterns for the configured GPIO register address list. In test_case(), chk_rst_val() is invoked first to iterate through addr_array[i] (i = 0..CNT-1). For each index, if skip_rst_array[i] == 1 the address is skipped; if read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000 the address is treated as not readable and skipped. Otherwise, data_rd = read_reg(addr), then data = (data_rd & 0xfffffffe) masks out bit 0 before comparison against default_value_array[i]. On mismatch, def_fail_cnt++ and an error is printed; on match, an optional PASS message is printed when DEBUG_DISPLAY is enabled. Next, chk_rd_wr() runs over six patterns via unsigned int chk_val[6] = {0xffffffff, 0xaaaaaaaa, 0x55555555, 0xf5f5f5f5, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xffff0000}. For each pattern, a write phase iterates i = 0..CNT-1: skip if skip_array[i] == 1, skip if write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000, otherwise write_reg(addr, (data_wr & write_mask_array[i])). Then a read/verify phase again iterates i: skip if skip_array[i] == 1; skip if write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000 or read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000; else data_rd = (read_reg(addr) & read_mask_array[i]); wr_n = (write_mask_array[i] ^ 0xffffffff); exp_val = ((data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | (wr_n & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i])). If data_rd == exp_val, an optional PASS message is printed when DEBUG_DISPLAY is enabled; otherwise wr_fail_cnt++ and a mismatch is printed. After both checks, test_case() calls finish(1) if (def_fail_cnt > 0 || wr_fail_cnt > 0), else finish(0). A soft_reset_chk() routine is present but excluded via #ifdef 0. The address list and all masks/defaults are provided by arrays in test_define.c.
Remarks: Registers flagged in the skip arrays are not exercised. Addresses with a zero read mask are not read; addresses with a zero write mask are not written. During default-value checking, bit 0 is ignored to prevent false mismatches. The soft-reset check code is disabled in this testcase.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1. For each register gp0_gpio_8 through gp0_gpio_27: if it is marked readable, read its value and compare against the documented default with bit 0 ignored; skip any entries marked to be skipped or not readable. 2. For each pattern in {0xFFFFFFFF, 0xAAAAAAAA, 0x55555555, 0xF5F5F5F5, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xFFFF0000}: for each register gp0_gpio_8 through gp0_gpio_27 that is writable, write the pattern masked by the register’s write mask; then read back the value masked by the read mask and verify that readable, writable bits match the programmed value and non-writable readable bits retain the default. 3. Record any mismatches and report the overall result.

Test Description: Validates level-triggered interrupt behavior for GP0 GPIOs 8–39. The test configures each pin for input with level interrupts, enables the group interrupt, stimulates the pin state via a memory-backed trigger, and verifies that the per-pin raw status asserts, the group status bit sets, and that both clear correctly when serviced. The sequence is repeated for both active-high and active-low level selections.
Meta Test Description: test_case(): 1) Optionally enable GIC interrupt line (87 for GPIO0 or 88 for GPIO1) under conditional compilation. 2) Enable the SoC system-level GPIO interrupt by writing to MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1 with either LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO0_INTR or LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO1_INTR (guarded by GPIO0/GPIO1). 3) For i = 0..31 (covering GPIOs 8–39): a) Compute wr_val = (1 << i). b) Program the per-pin configuration register at (MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + (i*4)) with 0x00180000 to select input mode and enable level interrupt (bits 20 and 19 set). c) wait_on(50). d) Enable the group interrupt bit by writing wr_val to MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1. e) wait_on(10). f) Write 0xffffffff to 0xA0243ffc to drive a memory-backed stimulus. g) Set int_pend = 1 and poll while (int_pend == 1), printing and wait_on(10) until the interrupt handler clears it. 4) wait_on(100). 5) Active-low selection pass: For i = 0..31 repeat: a) wr_val = (1 << i). b) Program (MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + (i*4)) with 0x00100000 (bit 20 = 1, bit 19 = 0) for input with level interrupt, active-low. c) wait_on(50). d) Enable the group interrupt by writing wr_val to MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1. e) wait_on(10). f) Write ~(wr_val) to 0xA0243ffc to stimulate an opposite level mask. g) Set int_pend = 1 and poll as above until ISR clears it. 6) finish(test_err). Default_IRQHandler(): 1) Set wr_val = (1 << i). 2) Clear int_pend (int_pend = 0). 3) Write 0xffffffff to 0xA0243ffc. 4) Read rdata = read_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + (i*4)). 5) If ((rdata & 0x2) != 0x0) then: a) Read rdata_grp = read_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1) and check ((rdata_grp & (1 << i)) != 0); else log error and increment test_err. b) Clear the per-pin raw status by writing 0x00110000 to (MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + (i*4)); wait_on(20); then read back rdata and verify rdata == 0x100001; else log error and increment test_err. c) Disable group interrupt by writing 0x00000000 to MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1. d) Read rdata_grp = read_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1) and verify rdata_grp == 0x0; else log error and increment test_err. e) If GPIO0: write MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1 with LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR, then read back MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1 and verify ((rdata & LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR) == 0); else increment test_err. If GPIO1: write MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1 with LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO1_INTR, then verify similarly. 6) Else (no raw status): print error and increment test_err. 7) Clear the corresponding GIC interrupt (87 or 88 based on GPIO instance).
Remarks: Requires platform routing of the GPIO interrupt to the GIC (IDs 87/88) and system interrupt enablement. The procedure relies on an ISR to service interrupts and on a memory-backed stimulus location to drive pin levels. Ensure access to the stimulus memory and that interrupts are globally enabled before running. Group interrupt must be enabled for each pin prior to validation.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1. Enable system-level and GIC interrupts for the GPIO block on the target platform. 2. For each of the 32 pins starting at gp0_gpio_8, configure input mode with level-triggered interrupt (active-high) and enable the corresponding bit in gp0_intr1_intr_en1. 3. Apply stimulus via the designated memory trigger and wait until the interrupt service routine completes. 4. Repeat the sequence for active-low selection by reconfiguring the same pins for low-level interrupt and re-enabling the corresponding group bits; apply complementary stimulus and wait for ISR completion. 5. During ISR handling, verify that the per-pin raw status asserts, the group status in gp0_intr1_intr_sts1 reflects the active pin, the per-pin status can be cleared and reads back as cleared, and the group status clears to zero when disabled. 6. Confirm that system-level interrupt status is cleared as part of ISR completion.
